ai.description: *Micrixalus kodayari* is a small frog (22–26 mm) with a brown dorsum and cream-colored belly. It is distinguished by a prominent white throat patch and the male's characteristic foot-flagging behavior.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Micrixalus kodayari* is best distinguished by its unique, vivid orange-red vocal sac, which contrasts sharply with the duller or paler throat coloration of other dancing frogs.
ai.habitat: *Micrixalus kodayari* inhabits high-elevation evergreen forests in the Southern Western Ghats, typically found near rocky, fast-flowing streams at altitudes above 1,000m.
ai.behavior: To attract mates, male *Micrixalus kodayari* perform a "foot-flagging" display, rhythmically extending and waving their hind legs to signal to rivals and potential partners.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Micrixalus kodayari* breeds during the monsoon, laying small clutches of eggs in hidden, gravel-filled nests beneath stream substrates.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Micrixalus kodayari* is endemic to the southern Western Ghats in Tamil Nadu, India, specifically inhabiting high-elevation streams in the Kodayar region.
ai.callDescription: The Kodayar Dancing Frog produces a high-pitched, short "chirp" repeated in rapid succession, typically heard near fast-flowing, rocky streams in the Western Ghats.
